items.title: DGFT extends RoDTEP support through 31 December 2026
items.summary: DGFT Notification 41/2026–27, dated 30 September 2026, continues RoDTEP through 31 December 2026 for eligible exports by DTA units, Advance Authorisation holders, SEZ units and EOUs. Existing rates and value caps remain unchanged.
content: DGFT has extended the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme until 31 December 2026 under Notification 41/2026–27, issued on 30 September 2026.
The extension covers eligible exports from Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) units, Advance Authorisation (AA) holders, Special Economic Zone (SEZ) units and Export Oriented Units (EOUs).
Rates and value caps under Appendices 4R and 4RE applicable on 30 September 2026 continue during this period. Other scheme terms and conditions also remain unchanged.
takeaways: Eligible DTA, AA, SEZ and EOU exports are covered.
Existing rates, value caps and other conditions continue.

items.title: Export consignments with FOB value up to ₹3 lakh are exempt from the RCMC / Certificate of Registration required
items.summary: FOB value from Rs. 1,00,000 increased to 3,00,000 for RCMC exemption
content:
S.O. (E): In exercise of powers conferred by Section 5 of Foreign Trade (Development &
Regulation) Act, 1992, read with paragraph 1.02 of the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023, as
amended from time to time, the Central Government hereby makes the following amendment
to the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023, with immediate effect:
In the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023, in paragraph 2.57, after sub-paragraph (b), the following
sub-paragraph shall be inserted, namely:-
(c) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) above, the requirement
of a Registration-cum-Membership Certificate or a Certificate of Registration shall not apply to
an export consignment where the Free-on-Board(FOB) value of the consignment does not
exceed₹3,00,000.
Effect of the Notification: With an objective to promote small value exports, especially
Exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels, this notification exempts export
consignments with an FOB value not exceeding 3,00,000 from the requirement of obtaining
RCMC or Certificate of Registration. Export consignments with an FOB value exceeding
3,00,000 shall continue to require a valid RCMC or Certificate of Registration wherever such
requirement is otherwise applicable under the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023.
a
This is issued with the approval of Minister of Commerce & Industry.

items.title: India's April–August exports reach an estimated US$399.27 billion
items.summary: India's combined merchandise and services exports reached an estimated US$399.27 billion during April–August 2026–27, up 15.55% year on year. Merchandise exports rose 17.85%, according to the Commerce Ministry's 15 September release.
items.source: Ministry of Commerce & Industry · PIB release dated 15 September 2026
content: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry's release of 15 September 2026 estimated India's combined merchandise and services exports at US$399.27 billion for April–August 2026–27. This compares with US$345.55 billion in the corresponding earlier period, an increase of 15.55%.
Merchandise exports reached US$215.91 billion, growing 17.85%. For August alone, combined exports were estimated at US$82.68 billion, up 25.41% year on year.

Electronics and engineering goods were among August's merchandise growth drivers, with increases of 89.82% and 24.86% respectively. Merchandise imports during April–August were US$363.00 billion, producing a goods trade deficit of US$147.09 billion.

The release notes that August services figures are estimated using available RBI data. Combined totals containing these estimates should be distinguished from merchandise-only figures and may subsequently be revised.
takeaways: Combined exports: estimated US$399.27 billion, up 15.55%.
Services figures include estimates and may be revised.

items.title: DGFT exempts export consignments up to ₹3 lakh from RCMC requirements
items.summary: DGFT has exempted export consignments with an FOB value of ₹3 lakh or less from RCMC or Certificate of Registration requirements under FTP 2023. The notification took effect on 15 September 2026.
items.source: DGFT Notification 36/2026–27, dated 15 September 2026 · Official copy hosted by APEDA
content: DGFT Notification 36/2026–27, issued on 15 September 2026, added paragraph 2.57(c) to the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 with immediate effect.

Under the amendment, an export consignment whose Free-on-Board (FOB) value does not exceed ₹3,00,000 is exempt from the policy's Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) or Certificate of Registration requirement.

The notification identifies small-value exports, including postal, courier and other emerging channels, as the focus of the measure. Consignments above ₹3,00,000 continue to require the relevant certificate wherever FTP 2023 otherwise requires it.

Exporters should review the linked notification when checking a shipment's eligibility. This exemption concerns registration certificates; it does not announce a general waiver of other export obligations.
takeaways: The threshold applies to each consignment's FOB value.
The relief covers RCMC or Certificate of Registration requirements.
Above ₹3 lakh, existing applicable requirements continue.
